steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Composition in photography is about what you INCLUDE and EXCLUDE from the frame — every element should have a purpose.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The rule of thirds places subjects at intersection points for dynamic balance; centre placement creates formality or stillness.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Leading lines guide the viewer's eye through the image — roads, fences, rivers, shadows all work as leading lines.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Viewpoint changes meaning: low angle = power; high angle = vulnerability; eye level = neutrality; dutch angle = tension.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring composition and framing. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with composition and framing. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with composition and framing. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to composition and framing, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
